samples.summary: Off-by-one in gate 1b's pagination: a PR with exactly 1000 changed files is refused even though the whole file list was read
samples.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` loops `page = 1..10` with `per_page=100` and only returns `false` when `files.length < 100`. A PR whose file list is exactly 10 full pages (1000 files) has been fully enumerated with no workflow path found, but the loop exits and falls through to `throw new Error("more than 1000 changed files — cannot rule out a workflow edit")` at line 194. `ranBaseCiDefinition` then catches that and returns `false`, so gate 1b fails and mark-ready exits 1 — a promotable PR is left as a draft on a boundary case that is actually fully readable. The correct terminator is `if (files.length < 100 || page === 10) return false;` (or a check that page 11 is empty).

samples.summary: Gate 1b reports a tooling failure (unreadable PR file list) as exit 1, which the new promote `case` records as `outcome=gates-unsatisfied` — the exact mis-attribution the outcome vocabulary was added to remove
samples.evidence: `ranBaseCiDefinition` catches ANY error from `branchEditsCiDefinition` (a 403/5xx/rate-limit from `pulls/{n}/files`, a `JSON.parse` failure) and returns `false`. That makes `allOk` false, so line 254-255 prints "Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied." and exits 1. The promote step's new `1)` branch (agent-review-panel.yml:1539-1542) sees the verdict line, writes `outcome=gates-unsatisfied`, and the job SUCCEEDS; loop-status then says "a ready gate was not satisfied — the PR stays a draft". A transient API failure is therefore reported as a gate verdict, with no page and no `tooling-error` outcome, and if no further push happens the PR sits as a draft indefinitely. This is the same class of mis-report the surrounding comment block (lines 1521-1527) says the outcome output exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The inline mirrors of `ciRunToRerun` are not equivalent to the exported function on inputs the pinning test never exercises (missing `id`, null elements)
samples.evidence: `checks.mjs:154` filters with `r?.status === "completed"` and orders with `(r.id ?? 0) > (newest.id ?? 0)`. The inline copies in agent-loop.yml:159-160 and agent-rerun.yml:203-204 use `r.status` (throws `TypeError` on a null/undefined element) and `r.id > n.id` (NaN → always false, so the FIRST run wins instead of the newest when `id` is absent). The cross-check in checks.test.mjs only feeds fixtures that always carry `status` and `id`, so the divergence the test claims to pin is not actually pinned. Low real-world impact (the Actions API always returns `id` and `status`), but the mirrors are not the same rule.

samples.summary: Switching from `per_page: 1` to "newest COMPLETED" can re-run a superseded run while a newer CI run for the same head SHA is still in flight
samples.evidence: Previously `runs.data.workflow_runs[0]` was the newest run regardless of status, so an in-flight run produced a 422 and the step became a documented no-op. Now `all.filter(r => r.status === 'completed')` skips the in-flight run and re-runs an OLDER completed one. If that older run is red and the in-flight one goes green, `agent-iterate-ci` (which fires on `conclusion == 'failure'`, agent-iterate-ci.yml:55) and the panel's `fix`/`promote` arms (which gate on `needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success'`) can both proceed for the same head SHA — the CI-conclusion MUTEX described in checks.mjs:180-186 is between arms watching the SAME run, and two runs for one SHA breaks it. Reachability requires a SHA to already carry two CI runs (checks.mjs:95-101 says only a close/reopen does this), so this is narrow, but the change removes the 422 that previously made it impossible.

samples.summary: Gate 1b's name and report line claim more than it checks: it proves the CI *workflow file* is main's, not that the tests CI runs are main's
samples.evidence: `CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES = ['.github/workflows/', '.github/actions/']`. But ci.yml executes `pnpm verify:self` etc. from the merge ref's own tree, so a branch that edits `harness.config.json`, `package.json` scripts, `scripts/verify*`, or any test runner still hands gate 1 a genuinely green run with the tests gutted — without touching any path in the prefix list. The gate is reported to the human as "CI ran main's definition" (line 238) and the hand-off comment asserts "that run executed the CI file on `main` rather than one the branch supplied" (lines 320-322), which is narrower than the name suggests. Grading minor because the check is a real improvement and the residual is the pre-existing state, but the label overstates the guarantee.

samples.summary: The new inline comment asserts something checks.mjs explicitly contradicts
samples.evidence: agent-loop.yml:147-148 and agent-rerun.yml:191-192 both say the newest completed run "is the run whose conclusion gate 1 reads". checks.mjs:136-139 states the opposite for the case that matters: "Note this is NOT always the run `ciConclusion` reads: with a newer run still in flight, gate 1 already answers `null`". The mirrored comments should carry the same caveat, since they are the copies a maintainer edits without checks.mjs open.

samples.summary: The proposed (not-yet-applied) `trigger-shape` canary can be silenced by the panel's own `noop` concurrency group
samples.evidence: The canary job in the staged patch has no `action`/`attempt` filter, so for a refused payload BOTH the `requested` and `completed` workflow_run events create panel runs — and both land in the `noop` concurrency group (agent-review-panel.yml:117) with `cancel-in-progress: true`, keyed only on head repo + branch. The earlier canary run is therefore cancelled rather than failing, and back-to-back refused runs on one branch can keep cancelling each other, so "the silence becomes a red run" is not guaranteed. A cancelled run is also not the visible red X the patch's rationale relies on.

finding.summary: Gate 1b reads the PR's diff against its OWN base branch, so a PR stacked on a branch that already gutted the CI definition passes the gate
finding.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` calls `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${number}/files`, which enumerates the diff of head against the PULL REQUEST'S BASE, not against `main`. The gate's stated invariant (mark-ready.mjs:20-29, and the report line at :238 "CI ran main's definition") only holds when base IS the default branch, and nothing in this script or in the promote job checks that: `pr view --json` at :122-128 never fetches `baseRefName`, and grep of scripts/agent finds no base-branch constraint anywhere on the promote path. Concretely: branch A edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to remove every test (PR A is refused by 1b, as intended, and just sits there); branch B is opened with base=A and contains only code. `pulls/B/files` returns no `.github/workflows/**` entry, `branchEditsCiDefinition` returns false, gate 1b passes — while B's `pull_request` CI run executed the merge ref of A+B, i.e. exactly the gutted ci.yml the gate exists to refuse. The panel itself does not share this blind spot (agent-review-panel.yml:455 diffs against `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`), so the two halves of the pipeline disagree about what "the branch changed" means, and 1b is the permissive one.

verdict.reason: The code is as the reviewer describes. mark-ready.mjs:183 enumerates changed files via `pulls/{number}/files`, which is the diff against the PR's OWN base, while the gate's reported invariant (mark-ready.mjs:238 and the hand-off text at :320-322) asserts the stronger "CI ran main's definition". mark-ready.mjs:122-128 requests only number,body,isDraft,labels,headRefName,headRefOid,url — `baseRefName`/`baseRefOid` are never fetched, and grep across scripts/agent finds no base-branch constraint on the promote path; the promote job (agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1509) passes only the PR number and required checks. The panel does anchor on main (agent-review-panel.yml:455, :459, :479), so the two halves of the pipeline disagree, with 1b the permissive one. I found a partial mitigation — ci.yml:9-10 limits `pull_request` to `branches: ["main"]`, so a PR based on a non-main branch gets no CI run and the workflow_run-triggered panel (agent-review-panel.yml:27-28) never fires — which defeats the literal A/B narrative. But it is not a guard on the gate: ciPassed (mark-ready.mjs:144-164) matches on head SHA alone, and the panel resolves the PR by head branch with `pulls.list({head: owner:branch})` taking data[0] with no base filter (agent-review-panel.yml:195-198), so a head branch with a second, later-created PR against a non-main base (or a PR retargeted after CI went green) can still hand gate 1b a base-relative file list while gate 1 reads a run built from a main merge ref. The gate never checks base, so I cannot name a guard that makes it unreachable.
